transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-29 16:00 PST
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Product), Ethan Marsh (GraniteBridge Platform Lead), Priya Nair (GraniteBridge ML Eng), Leah Brooks (GraniteBridge SRE), Omar Idris (GraniteBridge Data Ops)

Summary (auto):
Redwood ran through the Console Optimize walkthrough focused on savings heuristics — batching, prefix/KV cache strategies, and a cost model. Customer is evaluating tradeoffs for latency-sensitive market-data features and wants a sandboxed sim with their traffic. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted routing, encryption/KMS, and next steps for a short pilot.

Topics covered:
- Workload profile and token distribution
- Batching and concurrency knobs in Console
- Prefix (session) cache vs KV lookahead cache recommendations
- Cost model walkthrough and sensitivity sims
- Security gating for private trials

Transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: all right hey everyone thanks for joining, um I'm Maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off. Diego and Samir are here to walk through our optimize console and a savings model.
00:12 Ethan Marsh: thanks Maya, appreciate it. we pulled Priya and Leah in because this touches infra and model infra. quick ask — we want to see where we pencil in savings for our market insights product without blowing SLOs.
00:26 Diego Alvarez: perfect, that's the goal. quick intro: i'll focus on batching / cache heuristics and Samir will run the cost sim in the console. Maya will cover next steps and contract questions.
00:38 Priya Nair: just to flag — typical prompt is ~220 tokens, but we have a 2-step prompt for enrichment so head and tail lengths vary. latency budget is roughly 200ms p95 for interactive queries.
00:53 Diego Alvarez: ok that's helpful — 200ms p95 is tight. for that profile we tend to favor small continuous batching with aggressive prefix caching. with a 220 token average, full sequence generation is heavy, so you get the most wins from prefix / KV reuse.
01:10 Leah Brooks: can you spell out prefix versus KV again? sometimes the terms get fuzzy with our infra team.
01:15 Diego Alvarez: sure — prefix or session cache is storing the left context common across requests, like user profile or product metadata. KV lookahead is storing tokenized KV states for decoder reuse — the K and V caches for transformer attention that let subsequent calls avoid redoing compute. both reduce token cost but they trade differently on memory and hit characteristics.
01:37 Ethan Marsh: and the console shows both?
01:40 Samir Patel: yes, in Optimize -> Savings simulator we surface both — we call them Session prefix and KV lookahead. you'll see suggested hit rates based on your traffic shape; you can override to test scenarios.
01:52 01:54 Priya Nair: from our logs, about 70% of queries share the same initial 40 tokens, that's the potential prefix hit. but KV hits are trickier because downstream steps diverge.
02:07 Diego Alvarez: exactly, so the quick heuristic: if you have high prefix overlap (>50%), session caching gives large wins with minimal latency impact. KV lookahead gives bigger per-token computation savings but needs higher memory and consistent continuation patterns.
02:24 Maya Chen: let's pivot to a live demo in the console — Samir do you want to share the savings sheet link and the sandbox?
02:31 Samir Patel: sharing now, link: https://redwood.app/sandbox/granitebridge/sim-20270129 (note: link is demo only). and the savings spreadsheet: /drive/granitebridge/savings-model-v1.csv
02:45 03:05 Screen share starts, console visible
03:10 Samir Patel: here is the traffic profile editor — we uploaded a synthetic trace to match Priya's numbers. see tokens per request distribution, inter-arrival times, and current model variant.
03:24 Diego Alvarez: i'm toggling batch size and concurrency in the simulator. notice small batch size of 4 keeps latency within your 200ms p95 but reduces token cost by about 18% when combined with prefix cache at 60% hit.
03:40 Priya Nair: wait 18% seems high, what's the baseline?
03:44 Samir Patel: baseline is single-request no cache on hosted gen-large model. this sim uses our measured throughput kernels.
03:51 Leah Brooks: does that assume KV is on?
03:54 Diego Alvarez: that number was prefix-only. if we enable KV lookahead and we can sustain ~30% KV hit on multi-step flows, we push to ~32% token cost reduction but memory pressure goes up ~1.8x.
04:10 Omar Idris: memory pressure meaning GPU mem? and are we talking quantized models?
04:15 Diego Alvarez: yes GPU RAM for KV blobs, and we recommend int8/4-bit quant profiles where applicable to reduce memory. the console has suggested quantization profiles per model.
04:26 Ethan Marsh: what about Dedicated vs Hosted — do we need Dedicated to get predictable KV behavior?
04:31 Maya Chen: good question. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and reserved GPU memory profile, which helps with KV sizing and consistent hit behavior. Hosted can still do caching but fallbacks and routing may interleave other tenants so it's a bit less deterministic.
04:49 Priya Nair: any SLA differences or compliance gating we should know for a private trial?
04:54 Maya Chen: for private we can run VPC or on-prem options, key management via your KMS, SOC2 reports available. Samir can follow up with the security packet.
05:05 Samir Patel: sending security packet after the call; note the onboarding checklist link in the chat.
05:15 Diego Alvarez: returning to sim — i'm going to show sensitivity to concurrency. bump concurrency from 8 to 20, batch sizes grow and our per-token cost drops but latency p95 increases beyond your 200ms target.
05:33 Priya Nair: so it's a cost vs latency knob. we need a policy — keep p95 <=200ms and maximize savings. can console suggest an optimal point?
05:44 Samir Patel: yes we have a 'Latency SLO' slider. set to 200ms and the console auto-suggests batch size, concurrency, and prefix TTL to hit best cost under that constraint. here's a suggested policy: batch=6, concurrency=12, prefix TTL=30s, KV lookahead off (since your continuation patterns are low).
06:09 Ethan Marsh: interesting. how confident are those suggestions — are they model-verified or heuristic?
06:15 Diego Alvarez: they're built from our kernel selection models + historical runs: we run microbenchmarks per model family and use a performance model that estimates latency per batch and per-token cost at given concurrency. so it's a hybrid of measured profiles and heuristics.
06:30 Priya Nair: can we bring our exact model weights? we use an open-arch variant that's slightly customized.
06:36 Maya Chen: yes, for Dedicated or Private we can onboard your exact model build into the sandbox. for hosted we'd need to check compatibility for model artifacts but we often can run compatible variants.
06:48 06:50 Leah Brooks: about KV hit modeling, the console predicts hit rates — how do you calculate that?
06:56 Diego Alvarez: we infer hit-rate from token-prefix similarity and continuation entropy. you can upload sample traces and we run a short sim that tokenizes and computes expected reuse. it's probabilistic so we give ranges (low/expected/high).
07:17 Omar Idris: will the console change routing if hit rates are lower than expected? like fallback to non-KV to avoid latency spikes?
07:25 Samir Patel: yes, you can configure fallbacks: degrade KV usage or route to a lower-latency variant. Redwood supports automatic fallback policies in the rollout config.
07:36 Priya Nair: what about cost accounting — do we get token-level cost breakdowns?
07:40 Maya Chen: console shows token cost by generation vs KV recompute vs prefix rebuild. you can see token-level cost and per-route breakdown. it's also tied to invoices if you go hosted.
07:50 Ethan Marsh: is the savings sim exportable? we'd want to plug it into our finance model.
07:54 Samir Patel: yes CSV export — the sheet I linked contains scenario breakdowns and estimated monthly savings.
08:03 Diego Alvarez: quick note on TTLs — very short prefix TTLs increase requests to the prefix store and can add overhead; longer TTLs give more hit but stale state risk. for market signals, we usually choose 20–60s window.
08:21 Priya Nair: does Redwood handle eviction or do we need to implement a layer?
08:25 Diego Alvarez: Redwood will manage the cache with LRU and size-based eviction; you can also supply sticky session keys if you want affinity.
08:33 Ethan Marsh: security — is the prefix stored encrypted? and how about logs?
08:37 Maya Chen: prefix payloads can be encrypted at rest using your KMS, and audit logs are pushed to your SIEM in Private deployments. Hosted has managed logs with redaction options.
08:50 Leah Brooks: ok good. next steps recap?
08:54 Maya Chen: quick recap — Redwood will: send sandbox invite, share the annotated savings CSV (Samir/Diego), and run an initial sim on Priya's sample traffic. GraniteBridge will provide traffic traces and confirm security gating.
09:08 Ethan Marsh: timeline — can we do a 2-week pilot?
09:12 Maya Chen: yes we typically do 2-week sandbox pilots for econ sims. Diego: any other tech notes?
09:18 Diego Alvarez: one more: if you enable KV, plan for a sizing test — we run a short job to measure KV blob memory per concurrent session so you can size Dedicated pools.
09:30 Priya Nair: sounds good. thanks — we'll upload traces by Friday.
09:34 Maya Chen: great, we'll reconvene after Diego posts the initial sim results. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
